name: deciding a checkpoint
from: Work that continues because nobody stopped it: funded by momentum, its technical review verdict advisory to no one, every further hour spent by default rather than by decision.
to: A binding verdict — go, no-go, or redirect — taken at a named checkpoint, on a technical review that already passed and an independent quality opinion already heard, with what a go commits the firm to stated in a charter a stranger can read. Work that continues past the checkpoint continues because the firm chose it over everything else that hour could have bought.
cost: The decision itself — the deciders' attention on evidence they did not produce — and the killed work's sunk cost admitted out loud rather than ridden further.
otherwise: A firm with no office holding the trade-off does not stop doing things, which is the same as never having chosen to do them; the portfolio becomes whatever survived, and the money that went to what should have died was taken from what should have lived.
